name: Republic of the Congo

findings.controller: Huawei; Alcatel-Lucent (Nokia) Shanghai Bell; CMEC (contractors), China Eximbank (lender)
findings.local_actor: Government of the Republic of Congo
findings.summary: China Eximbank loans (2008, 2012, 2017) financed phases 1-2 of the National Coverage Project, a 3,000+ km fibre backbone linking Pointe-Noire, Brazzaville and Ouesso, built by Huawei, Shanghai Bell and CMEC; recorded as completed.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary), Chinese Development Finance dataset
AidData (William & Mary), Chinese Development Finance dataset
AidData (William & Mary), Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Date is the Pointe-Noire-Brazzaville segment's provisional acceptance; full completion date unknown per AidData. Announced value is the phase-1 commercial contract ($100m); phase-2 contract was $73m. All sources one host, so uncorroborated. Loans secured on SNPC oil proceeds.

findings.local_actor: Government of the Republic of Congo; Congo Telecom
findings.summary: Phase 3 of the National Coverage Project: Huawei contract signed July 2015, China Eximbank RMB 460 million concessional loan committed in 2017 alongside a separate preferential buyer's credit, extending fibre Ouesso-Impfondo and last-mile links.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary), Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4 because loan financing is committed; completion not confirmed. RMB value not converted to USD here (AidData's constant-2023 figure is about $72m, not an announced value). Audit 2026-10-22: 20 May 2017 belongs to the buyer's credit; 'still under implementation in 2022' not stated.

findings.summary: Phase 3 fibre works stalled after the oil-price fall left Congo struggling to service debt; the project resumed only after a 2019 debt-restructuring agreement, per AidData.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary), Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Coded as a pause (reversal) of the Phase 3 financing/construction; it was later resumed, so this is not a cancellation. Exact pause dates unknown.

findings.summary: MTN Congo ran a 5G pilot launched by the prime minister on 28 October 2022 with technical support from ZTE; the telecoms minister reported speeds above 10 Gbps.
findings.analyst_inference: MTN Congo announced commercial 5G in October 2024 (Techpoint Africa), but no source seen names the commercial RAN/core vendor.

findings.summary: The telecoms minister declared state-owned Congo Telecom's new mobile network operational after successful test calls with MTN and Airtel, citing a strategic partnership with Huawei.
findings.analyst_inference: Source names Huawei as partner but does not state it built or supplies the network; pole is provisional. Date inferred from the AllAfrica story ID; article gives only 23 December.

findings.controller: Government of the Republic of Congo (Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy
findings.financier: African Development Bank; Government of Congo
findings.summary: Brazzaville national data centre in Bacongo, funded by the AfDB and Congolese state under the Central Africa Backbone project and built by a Chinese contractor, missed 2024-2025 deadlines; inauguration now targeted before end-2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Controller coded domestic (state-owned facility); builder reported as Chinese (Construct Africa names Sumec and a second firm, truncated), operator not named. Announced value is Construct Africa's $15m; OSIRIS gives EUR 13.8m of the EUR 66.55m CAB envelope.

findings.controller: Government of the Republic of Congo
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy
findings.summary: The government signed a US$30 million agreement with India's Sterling and Wilson to build a data centre in Pointe-Noire under the Central Africa Backbone programme, with Exim Bank of India financing expected.
findings.analyst_inference: Controller coded domestic (government client); contractor and expected financier are Indian (third pole). Ecofin's '$30 billion' is evidently a typo for $30m. No later evidence of construction or operation was found.

findings.controller: China Academy of Information and Communications Technology (CAICT)
findings.local_actor: Government of the Republic of Congo
findings.summary: At a BRICS forum in Xiamen, Congo presented its Brazzaville-based Africa Research Centre for AI (operating since 2022 with the UN Economic Commission for Africa) and plans for a joint AI lab with China's CAICT.
findings.analyst_inference: Layer 'models' is the closest fit for an AI research centre; no model, compute or location named. CAICT is a PRC ministry-affiliated institute, hence pole prc. Statement of intent only. Audit 2026-10-22: CARIA has operated since 2022; only the CAICT joint lab is new and at planning stage.
